# Access Protected Members

#### Course: Learn C++ OOP

## Access Protected Members

Now let's see how we can access protected class members.

```cpp
1#include <iostream>
2using namespace std;
3
4class Person {
5    protected:
6        int id = 101;
7
8    public:
9        string name;
10};
11
12class Student : public Person {
13    public:
14
15
16        void access_protected() {
17            // access protected variable
18            cout << "ID: " << id << endl;
19        }
20
21};
22
23int main() {
24
25    // create an object of Student
26    Student student;
27    
28    // access the public variable of the parent class
29    student.name = "Jon Snow";
30    cout << "Name: " << student.name << endl;
31    
32
33    // call the access_protected() function
34    student.access_protected();
35
36
37    return 0;
38}
```

Output

```text
Name: Jon Snow
ID: 101
```

In the above example, we are accessing the protected variable inside the subclass Student.

```cpp
void access_protected() {
    cout << "ID: " << id << endl;
}
```

This is possible because protected variables can only be accessed by the same class or its subclasses.

![Protected members are accessible to derived classes.](data:image/png;base64,)

In order to access protected members outside the class and its subclasses, we must use public getter and setter functions (either inside the base class or inside the derived class) . Let's see how.
